Model dependence: Froustey and Pitrou (2405.06509), using full 3-flavor neutrino transport plus BBN, find that 'the space of allowed initial asymmetries is generically unbound' with current abundance and CMB data, because flavor equilibration is not complete in general and the CMB bound is at least quadratic in the asymmetries. So there is no single L_max. The L >~ 0.5-1 (2507.18752) and |L_alpha| ~ 0.1 with sum = 0 (2507.20659) windows depend on the initial flavor configuration at T >~ 20 MeV.

The tool grid (DW, m_s = 15, 20, 30, 40, 60 keV; sin^2 2theta = 1e-15 to 1e-11; 45 points) gives no BBN exclusion anywhere: |Delta chi^2_BBN| <= 0.0044 and Delta N_eff <= 3.4e-4. Only 60 keV at 1e-11 overcloses under DW (Omega h^2 = 0.22). Lifetimes run from 9.68e27 s (15 keV, 1e-12) to 9.45e23 s (60 keV, 1e-11). The grid CSV has no X-ray exclusion column, so I took the X-ray flags from predict_sterile_nu_xray_line.

Tool X-ray flags: (15 keV, 1e-12) is excluded by NuSTAR M31 (Roach+2020) and XMM blank sky (Dessert+2020), with Gamma = 1.03e-28 s^-1. (30 keV, 1e-13; Gamma = 3.31e-28), (40 keV, 1e-14; Gamma = 1.39e-28) and (60 keV, 1e-14; Gamma = 1.06e-27 s^-1) are all reported 'not excluded by tabulated limits (within 30% in mass)'. The tool's tabulated limits therefore do not reach the INTEGRAL/SPI or NuSTAR-GC regime above roughly 20-25 keV, so it cannot set the upper X-ray edge at 30-60 keV.

In the sterile-nu tool, the X-ray exclusion boundary at m_s = 20 keV lies between sin^2 2theta = 1e-13 (not excluded, Gamma = 4.36e-29 s^-1) and 1e-12 (excluded by NuSTAR M31, d-02). At 30 keV the tool flags nothing even at sin^2 2theta = 1e-11 (Gamma = 3.31e-26 s^-1, E = 15 keV). The tool therefore has no tabulated X-ray limit for line energies above about 10-13 keV (m_s >~ 25 keV), which explains why it cannot reproduce the NuSTAR-GC / INTEGRAL upper edge at 30-60 keV.

The m_th fit in 2507.18752 Eq. 8 has verbatim coefficients A = 1.329, a = 1.044, b = 0.055 (keV units), so at the paper's own benchmark (m_s = 37 keV, sin^2 2theta = 1.5e-14) m_th = 1.329 x 37^1.044 x (1.5e-14)^0.055 = 10.0 keV, not 8.6 keV. The f-002 value of 8.6 keV is an arithmetic error. The L fit (Eq. 9: C = 1.865e-12, alpha = -1.813, beta = -1.042) gives L = 0.68 at the same point, which confirms that part of f-002.

The consistent low-mass edge from m_th > 8.5 keV (Zelko+, 95% CL) uses the verified 2507.18752 Eq. 8: m_s,min = [8.5/(1.329 (sin^2 2theta)^0.055)]^(1/1.044) keV. By hand this gives m_s,min of about 36.5 keV at sin^2 2theta = 1e-15, 32.3 keV at 1e-14, 31.6 keV at 1.5e-14 and 28.6 keV at 1e-13.
